sections.title: Reading Comprehension · Passage B
sections.intro: Read “Naming the Birds” and answer questions 11–14.

passage.title: Naming the Birds
passage.credit: —W. Todd Kaneko · “Naming the Birds” · Orion Magazine, Summer 2020 · orionmagazine.org

lines.text: The beach is noiseless,
stretching behind my father’s house,
a mile of stones and driftwood
for those herons, ghostlike,
carefully picking their way
down the shoreline,
all knees and neck,
looking for crabs or something
they lost in the surf, and my father
points at them and says their names
like he is making a wish.
Then they are all gone and it’s just me
and the seagulls hover overhead
saying their own names,
the sky making those sounds
airplanes make when the world
has nothing left to say to you.
I have no memory of any wish
of mine coming true, no knowledge
of how a man turns to another man
and promises never to leave him,
but the other day I named the shadow
of a cardinal through a frosty window
for my son, described it so he would
know it when he sees one for himself.

questions.prompt: The herons’ searching for something “they lost” (line 9) implies

choices.text: the speaker’s admiration of their efforts
the speaker’s fears for their survival
a competition between the speaker and them
a parallel between the speaker and them

questions.explanation: The herons appear to search for something lost in the surf. Later the speaker recalls a father who is gone and admits he cannot remember a wish coming true, creating a parallel between their searching and his sense of loss.

questions.prompt: In the context of the poem as a whole, line 12 signals that the

choices.text: waves are forceful and the beach is calm
speaker is thinking about a past event
father is looking at the birds but not talking
birds are too far away for the speaker to hear

questions.explanation: “Then they are all gone and it’s just me” shifts from the remembered scene with the father and herons to the speaker's present solitude. It reveals that the earlier scene is a memory.

questions.prompt: The descriptions of the “herons” (line 4) and the “seagulls” (line 13) suggest a

choices.text: contrast between what is remembered and what is present
comparison between the habits of the two species
regard for the presence of such beautiful birds
recognition of the significance of the past and its lessons

questions.explanation: The herons appear in the remembered moment when the father is present; after they vanish, seagulls hover over the speaker alone. The two bird descriptions mark a contrast between remembered company and present solitude.

questions.prompt: The naming of the birds throughout the poem serves to
questions.explanation: The speaker's father once named the herons for him, and the speaker later names a cardinal for his own son. Repeating the act passes a bond across generations.
